title: From Vaccination Recommendations to Informed Decisions—A Mixed-Methods Study on Current Vaccination Counseling Practices in German Family Practices
summary:
Vaccinations are one of the most important ways of protecting against certain infectious diseases. However, whether or not someone gets vaccinated depends heavily on how well they are informed by their primary care physicians, who are among the most important providers of vaccinations in Germany, about the benefits and potential risks of vaccination. Currently, there is no comprehensive understanding of how family physicians in Germany provide information about vaccinations and how patients perceive it.
The planned study aims to address this gap by answering the following questions: 1) How accurately and comprehensively do family physicians inform their patients about the benefits and risks of vaccinations? 2) From GPs' perspectives, what factors influence the level of detail in the information provided? How do patients evaluate current information practices? Is the information understandable, transparent and sufficient? Do they feel taken seriously and treated as individuals? 4) What level of expertise do GPs have in assessing the benefits and risks of vaccinations?
Various research methods are being used to answer these questions: 1) Observations in general practice offices to see how counselling actually takes place. 2) Interviews with GPs about their experiences and beliefs. 3) Interviews with patients to gather their perspectives on the counselling. 4) A questionnaire survey of GPs to assess their expertise.
The aim is to develop a better understanding of how vaccinations are communicated in practice and how the counselling process can be improved. Effective shared decision-making, in which doctors and patients discuss the benefits and risks together, could enhance the quality of decision-making and increase acceptance of vaccinations, thereby improving vaccination rates in Germany.

interventions.name: Vaccination counseling provided by primary care physicians is being monitored as part of a participant observation study.
Interview with the family physicians who were observed as part of the participant observation study.
One-time questionnaire survey among family physicians

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Primary care physicians; 
Patients who have received vaccination counseling in the past two weeks.
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals under the age of 18, those who are acutely or permanently unable to give consent, and those with insufficient language comprehension. Individuals with impaired decision-making capacity are excluded. The primary care physicians who participated in the participant observation and interviews are excluded from the subsequent questionnaire survey.
